_comment: Permission allowlist for GATEWAY TURNS ONLY (KTD12).
Passed via `claude -p --settings daemon/permissions.json` by turn_runner;
it is NOT .claude/settings.json, so it never affects your interactive
sessions in this repo.
Why an allowlist instead of --dangerously-skip-permissions: a headless turn
cannot answer a prompt, and circuit-breaker prompts (rm -rf /) still fire
under bypass -- that would hang the turn forever while it holds the session
flock. bypass is also refused when running as root, which breaks portability
to other machines. Under dontAsk there are no prompts and no hang: anything
not allowed below fails the turn loudly, which is the behavior we want.
VERIFIED 2026-07-28 against real turns. Two findings shaped these rules:
(a) A command containing SHELL-VARIABLE EXPANSION is denied regardless of
the allowlist -- the matcher cannot know what $PY expands to. CLAUDE.md
therefore tells the brain to write this interpreter path literally.
(b) The tilde form below matched a real invocation; the same rule written
with the expanded /Users/... path did NOT. Keep the tilde form, and
keep rule and command spelled the same way.
HONEST SCOPE: this is not a sandbox. The brain legitimately runs inline
python (`python3 -c ...`), so allowing it is equivalent to allowing arbitrary
code. What this list actually buys: no prompts, no headless hang, portability
off this machine, and a deny-list for the few genuinely destructive verbs.
The real security boundary remains the owner-gated transport plus the
owner-allowlisted send path (U8), not this file.
MAINTENANCE: a missing rule does NOT fail the turn -- verified 2026-07-28:
the turn exits 0 and the model narrates the denial. The turn runner therefore
treats send-evidence, not exit status, as delivery truth. The U11 parity suite
runs real turns and is the gate that proves this list complete.
That gate earned its keep immediately: the rotation drill caught Edit being
allowed on session-handoff.md ALONE while Write was allowed on all of
state/** -- an arbitrary split, since the model picks Edit for a file that
already exists. The nightly flush edits an existing file, so the split would
eventually have silently dropped a night of context (rotation is silent, so
there is no send-evidence to catch it; rotate() now verifies the file's
mtime instead). Both verbs now cover state/**.
Scope note: first-instance has no MCP servers -- the brain drives local
scripts. An instance that DOES use MCP adds e.g. "mcp__whoop__*".
